papers.title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

papers.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(\Omega) \le \frac{\pi^{s-\frac{1}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)\Gamma\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partial\Omega)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator
papers.abstract: We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average. The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

papers.title: Polynomial Spaces Are Locally Paley-Wiener: Bulk Universality and Christoffel Asymptotics on Symmetric Convex Bodies
papers.abstract: We prove a bulk universality limit for total-degree polynomial spaces on symmetric convex bodies. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density near an interior point, the rescaled reproducing kernel converges to the Fourier integral over the dual unit ball of the Baran metric, which we call the local spectral body. After diagonal normalization, the limit is the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on this body. The result holds uniformly on compact subsets where the local density assumption holds and yields the corresponding Christoffel asymptotic. Its main constructive ingredient is recovery, with the exact rescaled $L^2$ norm, of Paley-Wiener functions at arbitrary interior centres by Chebyshev ridge polynomials. This extends the classical polynomial-entire function limit at the symmetry centre to a position-dependent local spectrum. Ellipsoidal spectral bodies recover the known Bessel profile on the ball; polytopal spectral bodies give other Fourier profiles. For rectangles, the two-dimensional profile is a product of two sinc functions. On a regular hexagon, the local spectral body changes from a hexagon to a parallelogram across the inscribed circle; explicit Fourier profiles are available in both regimes. The proof uses the Siciak extremal function and does not require a differential operator or an explicit orthogonal-polynomial kernel.

papers.title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of the Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + a(t)g(u)=0,\qquad u'(0)=u'(T)=0, \] with a two-step sign-changing weight. Under an explicit condition on an increasing nonlinearity \(g\), we prove that for every prescribed integer \(N\ge 1\) and every prescribed ratio \(\kappa>0\) of the step lengths, there exist step weights of that ratio and strictly negative integral for which the problem has at least \(N\) distinct positive solutions. The multiplicity persists under small perturbations of the weight parameters. A structural condition on \(g'/g\) yields at least three positive Neumann solutions for \(g(u)=e^{u^p}-1\) for every \(p>1\). An explicit increasing nonlinearity also satisfies the \(N\)-solution criterion for every finite \(N\), with the weight chosen separately in each case.

papers.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
papers.abstract: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

papers.title: Nonlinear Fourier series
papers.abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

papers.title: It\^o formula for planarly branched rough paths
papers.abstract: The It\^o formula is a cornerstone of stochastic calculus, providing a fundamental change-of-variables formula for stochastic processes. In rough path theory, It\^o formulas have been proved for rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{3}< \alpha \leq \frac{1}{2}$ and branched rough paths with roughness $0< \alpha \leq 1$. Planarly branched rough paths provide a natural framework for studying rough differential equations on homogeneous spaces, extending the theory of branched rough paths through the Munthe-Kaas-Wright Hopf algebra. In the present paper, we prove the It\^o formula for planarly branched rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{4}< \alpha \leq \frac{1}{2}$.

papers.title: Variational estimates for discrete spherical averages: $\ell^p$-boundedness and related arithmetic obstructions
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate variational inequalities for the family of discrete spherical averages. We establish $\ell^p$-boundedness of the $r$-variation operators for $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$ along sufficiently sparse sequences of factorial radii. Moreover, we also study arithmetic obstructions to these variational estimates and construct counterexamples to show that such boundedness properties for the corresponding variational operators cannot hold for lacunary sequences of radii.

papers.title: Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and H\'elein applies.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schr\"{o}dinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schr\"odinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: Generic local identifiability for ODE inverse problems from discrete observations
papers.abstract: We study local parameter identification from finitely many measurements of an analytic output along a single ODE trajectory. At a fixed initial state and parameter, the time derivatives of the output sensitivity define a decreasing sequence of parameter kernels. If the sequence reaches zero, any prescribed pattern of distinct positive sampling times gives full parameter rank after a sufficiently small common rescaling, provided the number of times is at least the number of strict kernel drops. The orders of these drops determine the asymptotic orders of all singular values of the sampled Jacobian. We also give a sharp worst-case bound on the number of freely chosen observation times needed for the sampled Jacobian to have full column rank. At a generic point, the maximum parameter rank determines how many local parameter coordinates can vary without changing the observations. A quantitative inverse estimate bounds the error of every estimate in the certified neighborhood that fits the data at least as well as the true parameter. For a \(d\)-dimensional homogeneous linear system with known initial state and \(d\) equally spaced positive-time full-state observations, cyclicity for the sampled propagator is equivalent to local identifiability of the generator. In this case, one additional exact full-state sample at a time incommensurate with the grid spacing gives global recovery.

papers.title: A hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan, its validity range and implications
papers.abstract: We extend the validity range of a hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan proved by Berndt, Bhargava and Garvan [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 347, 4163 (1995)] and study its implications. Relations to special values of complete elliptic integrals of the first kind in singular value theory are established. Consequently, we derive several closed-form evaluations of hypergeometric functions $_2F_1$ with different sets of parameters and arguments. Connections with other hypergeometric transformations and some recent results are discussed.

papers.title: Weighted boundedness for the maximal operator associated with matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness on $L^p(w)$ of the maximal operator $M_{A^{-1}}$, defined by $M_{A^{-1}}f(x)=Mf(A^{-1}x)$, that is, the maximal of Hardy-Littlewood composed with a invertible matrix $A$. We present two different results of boundedness and provide a characterization for a particular case of matrices. The main novelty lies in examples illustrating the difference between the class of weights with a matrix, $\mathcal{A}_{A,p}$, and the classical Muckenhoupt weight class, $\mathcal{A}_{p}$. Finally, we extend these results to the fractional framework, considering the fractional maximal operator $M_{\alpha, A^{-1}}$.

papers.title: Optimal constants of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators
papers.abstract: We study optimal constants and extremizers of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators. In particular, we establish harmonic oscillator analogues of free particle results due to Simon (1992), Bez and Sugimoto (2015), and Bez et al. (2015).

papers.title: A Resurgent Analytic Framework for Indicial Umbral Calculus via Mellin-Barnes and Borel-Laplace Theories
papers.abstract: We introduce the Analytic Umbral Framework (AUF), which gives formal indicial umbral evaluation an analytic meaning through Mellin-Barnes pairings. An auxiliary Borel representative defines a continuous linear action on compatible weighted spaces of analytic ground states. The resulting function is initially defined in a sector of the logarithmic covering. Finite contour displacement recovers the formal umbral coefficients, with remainder estimates distinguishing ordinary asymptotics, strong Gevrey asymptotics and equality with a convergent series. The associated auxiliary Laplace series are resurgent for rational profiles and entire profiles of exponential type. Under explicit spectral conditions, the pairing coincides with the Borel-Laplace sum of the evaluated formal series. An exact spectral transmutation relates exponential and rational representatives and extends to admissible P\'olya superpositions. It preserves the analytic value under a compensating change of ground state. A Hankel construction supplies complementary realizations for inverse-Gamma states. Worked examples involving special functions illustrate convergent and divergent evaluations, logarithmic expansions and the justification of operational integration. In the zero-dimensional quartic model, a single pairing yields the weak- and strong-coupling expansions and an exact nonperturbative lateral connection.

papers.title: Continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation on the integers and the real numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, the continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation \[ f_1 ( u + v ) f_2 ( u - v ) f_1 ( u' + v' ) f_2 ( u' - v' ) = f_1 ( u + v' ) f_2 ( u - v' ) f_1 ( u' + v ) f_2 ( u' - v ) \] are classified for $ \mathbb{ Z } $ and $ \mathbb{ R } $. By using this classification for $ \mathbb{ Z } $, we consider a generalization of the Kac--Bernstein theorem on the one-dimensional torus $ \mathbb{ T } $ by Baryshnikov--Eisenberg--Stadje from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures. Similarly, the original Kac--Bernstein theorem on $ \mathbb{ R } $ is generalized from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures.

papers.title: Semi-Discrete Linear Hyperbolic Curvature flow
papers.abstract: We consider evolution of piecewise linear curves with boundary by linear hyper- bolic curvature flows in which each interior vertex accelerates in proportion to its discrete curvature. The flow can be equally considered as a damped wave equation on a path graph or alternatively a damped mass-spring chain. The anal- ysis rests on the spectral theory of the Dirichlet path Laplacian, a tridiagonal Toeplitz matrix and an associated quadratic eigenvalue problem. Given appropri- ate boundary behaviours we find corresponding self-similar solutions and more generally, given any specific boundary trajectories we write down general solu- tions using finite Fourier expansions. We also consider the problem of evolving one piecewise linear curve to another using nonhomogeneous linear hyperbolic flow. Finally we discuss anisotropic variants and more general mass-spring systems.

papers.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
papers.abstract: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet $L^2$-norm. The zero-dimensional case yields a large-value estimate on $R^{1/2}$-cubes. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.
